layout_dets.text: CONCLUSIONS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HS steel has a higher trap density than LS steel. This conclu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion follows from the greater quantity of nonmetallic inclusions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (mostly sulfides) contained in HS steel than in LS steel, and also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the greater amount of hydrogen absorbed by HS steel than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by LS steel under identical charging conditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Both steels suffer losses of ductility after charging. LS steel suf-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fers an irreversible loss of ductility, while HS steel regains its duc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tility after 120 hours of aging.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inclusion/matrix interfaces are strong trap sites that are still op-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erative at 250°C.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The trapping energy of inclusion/matrix interfaces is greater in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LS steel than in HS steel. This conclusion follows from almost the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same hydrogen contents found in both steels after 120 hours of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aging despite the higher trap density in HS steel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During aging, the inclusion/matrix interfaces in both steels trap

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hydrogen taken from both the lattice and weak traps.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The pitting susceptibility of a range of austenitic stainless steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with different molybdenum contents was evaluated in both chlo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ride and bromide solutions at elevated temperatures, using elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trochemical polarization techniques. It is found that there is a less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: beneficial effect of molybdenum in solutions containing bromide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions than in those with chloride. Particular attention has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paid to the pitting behavior of UNS(¹)S31254 steel, which is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found to be significantly more susceptible in bromide solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effects of inclusions has also been observed on this alloy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effect of molybdenum on pitting corrosion resistance in differ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent aggressive solutions is discussed, and it is suggested that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interaction of molybdenum with specific aggressive anions should

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be taken into account in developing possible mechanisms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through which this alloying element improves the pitting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of iron-based alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: KEY WORDS: bromide, pitting, stainless steel.

layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Submitted for publication November 1988; revised February 1989.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The breakdown of passivity, which leads to localized corrosion, is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a common type of failure of stainíess steels. The pitting behavior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of stainless steels has been studied extensively in environments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing aggressive ions similar to those found in their operating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments, and reviewed by Smialowska,1 Galvele,² and Janik-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Czachor et al.³ However, most work has been done in solutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing chloride as the aggressive ions. This is presumably be-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cause chlorides are most commonly encountered in environments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as seawater, pulp and paper processing, and chemical plants

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in general. It is believed that chlorides are the most aggressive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anions for the pitting corrosion attack of stainless steels.

layout_dets.text: EXPERIMENTAL

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Materials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The series of austenitic stainless steels with different molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum contents shown in Table 1 were used in anodic polariza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion-controlled experiments. UNS S30100, UNS S31600, and UNS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: N08904 samples were cut from cold-rolled sheets, and UNS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: S31254 samples were taken from tube material. Two heats of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: UNS S31254 materials were tested because Heat 1 material was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found to contain a significant quantity of titanium-rich inclusions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and was thus metallographically less clean than Heat 2 material.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The pitting susceptibility of autogeneously welded zones, both an-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nealed and unannealed, of UNS S31254 tubes was also studied.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The samples used for potentiodynamic measurements were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface ground to 600 grade silicon carbide paper, with additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine polishing used for samples to be examined by optical or elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tron optical microscopy. Details of sample preparation can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found elsewhere.⁶

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Solutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Chloride, bromide, and mixed neutral (pH ~ 7) solutions were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prepared from analytical reagents, sodium salts, and distilled wa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ter. The ratios of [Br−]([Br] + [Cl-]) were chosen as 0.25, 0.50,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 0.75 for bromide-chloride mixed solutions, with a fixed total

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration [Br⁻] + [Cl] = 0.6 M. Test solutions were deaera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ted by nitrogen for one hour prior to the beginning of and for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duration of experiments.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Procedures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiodynamic measurements were carried out to deter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mine pitting potentials and critical temperatures for pitting. Poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tiodynamic polarization commenced at the free-corrosion potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: after the sample had been immersed in the solution for 30 min-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: utes, using a scan rate of600 mV/h.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Potentiostatic polarization for microscopic examination of pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: morphology, pit distribution and inclusion behavior was conducted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by holding the sample at a potential higher than the pitting poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial. An optical and a Philips(²) model 515 scanning electron micro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scope were used to examine samples after potentiostatic treat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: No theory has taken into consideration the specific interaction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CONCLUSIÓNS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: UNS N08904 and UNS S31254 are more susceptible to pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion in bromide than in chloride, as evidenced by the relative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting potentials and the “critical pitting temperatures."

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Variations in cleanliness of UNS S31254 affect the pitting resis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tance in bromide solution, and the nucleation of pits at titanium-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rich inclusions occurs, but there is little commensurate change in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the measured pitting potentials.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There is a specificity in the action of molybdenum in controlling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion in the presence of chloride and bromide, suggest-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing that the mechanism of this action is related to the detailed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chlorine or bromine chemistry of molybdenum.
